Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=5,$ calculate the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A)=5.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AC} \\ 5 & =\frac{2x+4}{x-1} \\ 5(x-1) & =2x+4 \\ 5x-5 & =2x+4 \\ 3x & =9 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x+4=2(3)+4=10, \\ AC & =x-1=3-1=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 10 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 16\cdot 10 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/6b6385bfeb341402b8a9bcc3668a095c7dcf82cff111273275598a971e0d156b.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal A = \dfrac 1 2 AC \cdot BC.
$$

Notice that relative to the given angle $\angle B,$ we have the length of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and need to determine the length of the adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $BC{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({60}^{∘}) & =\frac{9}{BC} \\ \sqrt{3} & =\frac{9}{BC} \\ \sqrt{3}BC & =9 \\ BC & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{3}}{3} \\  & =3\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 9\cdot (3\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{27\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that $\tan(m\angle{B}) =\dfrac{4}{3},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/ac4681632fd3f38f6d61a15fada02054eef264c37aaf6039465e93fc3954dbf5.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 BC \cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\tan(m\angle{B}) = \dfrac{4}{3}.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{B},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \frac{4}{3} & =\frac{2x+2}{2x} \\ 4\cdot 2x & =3\cdot (2x+2) \\ 8x & =6x+6 \\ 2x & =6 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =2x+2=2(3)+2=8, \\ BC & =2x=2(3)=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 8 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that $\sin \theta = \dfrac 13,$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/3acaffefa93ecbf278a6126661fb9b128ed4f904a22306acd32289eef46d2e0a.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\sin \theta = \dfrac13,$ where $\theta = m\angle{A}.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overline{BC}$ opposite to $\angle{A}.$ Hence, we can use the sine ratio to find the length of the hypotenuse $\overline{AB}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \frac{1}{3} & =\frac{5}{AB} \\ AB & =5(3) \\ AB & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the Pythagorean theorem to find the missing side $AC\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\sqrt{A{B}^{2}-B{C}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{15}^{2}-{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{225-25} \\  & =\sqrt{200} \\  & =10\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 10\sqrt{2}\cdot 5 \\  & =25\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
\mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m\angle{B} = 23^\circ.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{B},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘}) & =\frac{x-1}{2x} \\ 2x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘}) & =x-1 \\ 1 & =x-2x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘}) \\ 1 & =x(1-2\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘})) \\ x & =\frac{1}{1-2\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({23}^{∘})} \\ x & =6.620\,3…\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x=2(6.620\,3…)=13.240\,6…, \\ AC & =x-1=(6.620\,3…)-1=5.620\,3….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(5.620\,3…)(13.240\,6…) \\  & =37.208\,0… \\  & ≈37.2,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the one decimal place.

tutorials.problem:
Consider the right triangle $\triangle ABC$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/3f7de9810f4acf33b504eb010d641e99811de82eed919e4340b5e68d414269ca.png)

The area of this right triangle is

$$
\mathcal A = \dfrac 1 2 ab.
$$

But how can we calculate the area if we only know one side and one angle, as in the triangle below? 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/c1e5331333639f4d8e4f7b4cb3fee30ed1a7a889968844ae2b10961c5ae8e3ef.png)

We can follow the two steps below.

**Step 1**: Calculate the missing side using the trigonometric ratios.

Here, we need the adjacent side, and we know the opposite side. So, we should use tangent:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘} & =\frac{3}{BC} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} & =\frac{3}{BC} \\ BC\sqrt{3} & =9 \\ BC & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{3}} \\ BC & =3\sqrt{3}\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Use the formula to calculate the area.

Now that we know both sides of the triangle, we can just apply the formula as usual and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 3\sqrt{3} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{3}}{2}\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the right triangle $\triangle ABC$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/3f7de9810f4acf33b504eb010d641e99811de82eed919e4340b5e68d414269ca.png)

The area of this right triangle is

$$
\mathcal A = \dfrac 1 2 ab.
$$

But how can we calculate the area if we only know one side and one angle, as in the triangle below? 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14226474/assets/c1e5331333639f4d8e4f7b4cb3fee30ed1a7a889968844ae2b10961c5ae8e3ef.png)

We can follow the two steps below.

**Step 1**: Calculate the missing side using the trigonometric ratios.

Here, we need the adjacent side, and we know the opposite side. So, we should use tangent:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘} & =\frac{3}{BC} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} & =\frac{3}{BC} \\ BC\sqrt{3} & =9 \\ BC & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{3}} \\ BC & =3\sqrt{3}\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Use the formula to calculate the area.

Now that we know both sides of the triangle, we can just apply the formula as usual and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 3\sqrt{3} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{3}}{2}\,{\text{cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
